title: Pizza Quattro Formaggi
subtitle: Four-cheese pizza without tomato
excerpt: Pizza Quattro Formaggi is a white pizza topped with four melted cheeses: mozzarella, gorgonzola, fontina, and parmesan. There is no tomato sauce. The result is rich and a little salty, with each cheese contributing a different texture and flavour.
sourceNotes: The four-cheese pizza is a standard of Italian pizzerias across all regions. The choice of cheeses varies widely, but gorgonzola, mozzarella, and parmesan are the most consistent pairing. Fontina is the standard fourth cheese in northern Italy; taleggio, provolone, and scamorza are common alternatives in other regions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the dough 24 hours ahead. Grate the parmesan and slice the other cheeses just before topping.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan or conventional, maximum oven setting. Preheat with a heavy tray or pizza stone inside for at least 45 minutes.

content.text: Pizza Quattro Formaggi is a white pizza, meaning there is no tomato sauce. The base gets four cheeses instead: mozzarella, gorgonzola, fontina, and parmesan. Each melts differently. The mozzarella stretches and pools, the gorgonzola spreads into puddles with a sharp, salty edge, the fontina becomes smooth and creamy, and the parmesan stays in slightly browned, savory patches. The result is rich, so portions are slightly smaller than a tomato pizza.
You need one 210 g ball of 24-hour pizza dough per pizza, rested at room temperature for 2 hours before shaping.
Heat the oven to its maximum setting with a heavy tray or pizza stone on the top shelf. Preheat for at least 45 minutes.
Stretch one dough ball to a rough 30 cm disc, leaving a 2 cm border at the edge. Do not add tomato sauce.
Scatter the mozzarella over the base, then dot the gorgonzola over the top. Lay the fontina slices evenly across the disc. Sprinkle the parmesan over everything. Drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the rim is charred and the cheese is melted and bubbling with golden patches. Add a crack of black pepper as you take it out of the oven. Eat immediately.

The four-cheese pizza is a standard across Italy rather than a dish tied to a single region. The cheese combination changes depending on what is local. In Lombardy you might find taleggio in place of fontina; in Campania, provolone. The version here uses the most widely available four-cheese combination and can be adapted to whatever is in the fridge.
